title: Seasonal bias correction gave no clear six-month ENSO forecast gain at 2000-2024 origins
abstract: We tested a seasonal correction of past errors in six-month ENSO probability forecasts. We reused revised NOAA ERSSTv5 temperature and GODAS warm water volume records. At 300 monthly origins in 2000-2024, annual-harmonic bias correction raised mean negative log density from 0.94223 to 0.97251 nats. Gain was -0.03028 nats. Conditional 95% limits were -0.06467 to 0.00165 with three-year blocks and -0.06158 to -0.00324 with five-year blocks. Mean squared error rose by 5.04%. Constant bias correction also gave no clear gain. The evidence for a loss depends on the block rule. This test does not support the added correction for this model and period. It does not identify a physical cause or show that all bias corrections fail. Few ENSO cycles, revised inputs, normal distributions and conditional intervals limit inference. Code, hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure and an audit are included.
